items.body: Today the caret on `Some` answers `Option<RemoteStoreSome<Global>>::Some(RemoteStoreSome<Global>)` and Option's `Some` doc (E241). The owner wants the arm's tooltip upgraded; the recommended shape, for the owner to confirm or amend: ONE fenced `vilan` block of up to three lines - (1) `match on Option<RemoteStoreSome<Global>>` (the subject's type, so a reader sees what is being matched without scrolling to the head), (2) the variant line as E241 writes it, (3) the binding(s) the leg introduces as declarations, `let root: RemoteStoreSome<Global>` (a tuple/struct payload one line per capture; `_` and literal legs omit it) - then the variant's `///` as the Doc block, and, where the subject's type carries a `[hint(Trait<..>)]` abbreviation (vilan.inlayHints.abbreviate), the abbreviated spelling the inlay hints use so the two agree. An `is` pattern (`if v is Some(let x)`) answers the same. The `_` leg keeps E241's `_: T` plus the subject line. Door: `pattern_labels` already carries the variant and the payload; the captures' binding labels are what the inlay hints print (`inlay_hints` at ~4771; the capture-name anchoring pin at ~30231); the subject's type is the `match` expression's slot. Pins: the kolt shape (an Option over a nominal with arguments), a tuple payload with two captures, a struct variant, `_`, an `is`, an inline transient subject, a leg whose variant carries a `///`. Sizing S (vilan-lsp document.rs `pattern_hover`; a label field or two in vilan-core's `pattern_labels`).

items.title: an INLAY HINT's tooltip is the binding's hover, syntax-highlighted — hovering the `: RemoteStoreSome<Global>` hint after `Some(let root)` (kolt views.vl:187) shows the bare string `RemoteStoreSome<Global>` with NO highlighting, because the server sends `InlayHintTooltip::String`; it should send a fenced `vilan` block with the declaration (`let root: RemoteStoreSome<Global>`) and the type's own hover (its declaration head and `///`), with the hint's type name clickable to its definition
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-10-12/13): `Some(let root) => <div` with the inlay hint after `root` marked "here (see views.vl:187)" - "currently shows `RemoteStoreSome<Global>` with no syntax highlighting on hover"; vilan-lsp main.rs ~5052 (`tooltip: hint.full.map(|full| InlayHintTooltip::String(full))`, the `: `/` as ` prefix trimmed - E278); the test helper at main.rs ~6867 that PANICS on a `MarkupContent` tooltip ("a plain tooltip") - the pin to turn around; `Document::binding_hover` (what the binding's own name answers: fenced, with E221's lead); E278 (a stage hint's ` as T` tooltip - the same change applies); E300 (the match arm hover - the capture's declaration line is shared)
items.body:
The tooltip becomes `InlayHintTooltip::MarkupContent` (markdown) carrying what the binding's NAME would hover: a fenced `vilan` block with the typed declaration (`let root: RemoteStoreSome`; for a stage hint, the stage's expression text elided to `… as Option`), then the TYPE's hover under it - the nominal's declaration head (`struct RemoteStoreSome

` / `enum Option`) and its `///` - so a reader learns what the type IS from the hint without a second hover; the Platform and Diagnostic (E221) blocks as the name's hover carries them. The label becomes `InlayHintLabel::LabelParts` with the type NAME part carrying `location` (the nominal's definition - a click goes there) and the same tooltip; the abbreviated `~Source<..>` spelling (vilan.inlayHints.abbreviate) keeps its tooltip as the FULL type on the first line (E278's rule) above the rest. Cost: the tooltip is built from labels the hover already has; the keystroke `inlay` row of lsp-latency must not move (E121: <10 ms). Pins: the kolt shape, a stage hint, an abbreviated hint, the label part's location, the markdown fence present, the main.rs helper updated. Sizing S (vilan-lsp main.rs + document.rs).

items.title: an OPT-IN chain inlay-hint strategy, `vilan.inlayHints.chains = "changes"`, hints a stage of a multi-line chain only where its type DIFFERS from the previous stage's — `Some(5)` / `.map(|x| x * 2) as Option<i32>` / `.and_then(|x| Some(x + 1))` (hidden: still `Option<i32>`) / `.is_some() as bool` — against today's one hint per stage (E278)
items.discussion: the owner's ask (2026-10-12/13) with the four-line example; E278 (a hint per STAGE of a chain split one stage per line, spelled ` as T`; the "Ascribe every stage of this chain" action - document.rs ~4833, ~4946; pins `a_three_stage_chain_hints_each_line` ~32054, `inlay_hint_abbreviates_an_iterator_adapter_chain` ~31911); `vilan.inlayHints.enabled` / `.abbreviate` in editors/vscode/package.json (~121) and the server's settings reader; E301 (the hint's tooltip)
items.body: A new setting `vilan.inlayHints.chains`: `"every"` (today's behaviour, the default) | `"changes"` (opt-in): in a chain split one stage per line, a stage's ` as T` hint is shown when its type differs from the PREVIOUS stage's and hidden when it is the same - the first hinted stage always shows (there is no previous), the last stage shows when it differs from its predecessor (`.is_some() as bool`), and a hidden stage still counts as the predecessor for the next comparison. "Same" is judged on the type as the hint would PRINT it after abbreviation (so `~Source<Option<str>>` twice is the same), not on the slot id; a chain whose every stage is the same type shows the first only. The "Ascribe every stage" action (E278) is unchanged - it ascribes every stage, hidden ones included (the hints are a view; the ascription is the code); its title says so. Applies live (the setting is read per request like `abbreviate`). Pins: the owner's four-line example (2 of 3 stage hints shown), every-stage-same (1 shown), a chain on one line (no hints, unchanged), the default unchanged (E278's pins stand), the action ascribing all. Sizing S (vilan-lsp document.rs's chain hint pass + the settings plumbing + package.json + the extension's README line).
